subject: Developer Experience Bridge: LangChain & LlamaIndex SDK compatibility check
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Developer Experience Bridge: LangChain & LlamaIndex SDK compatibility check

Hi Elena / ToolSmith integrations team,

Following up from last quarter's partner forum — we want to run a short, lightweight compatibility and certification check for the "Developer Experience Bridge" (DX Bridge) so ToolSmith's SDKs and sample integrations are verified against Redwood's tracing and initialization patterns. The goal is to create a reproducible checklist and a small test harness so ISV devs can validate compatibility on their side before certification.

High level ask: can you commit to a 2-week joint validation window the week of Feb 22 to Feb 28? Deliverables we'd like to produce together:
- a checklist (instrumentation surface, init patterns, env flags)
- a small trace harness (OTel-compatible) that exercises: model load, streaming tokens, fallback routing
- a short conformance run (10 sample prompts + one latency regression smoke test)

Attached is a first draft of the certification requirements and a reference harness we maintain. Can you confirm the proposed window and point us to the engineer on your side who will join the validation sprint?

Thanks — I can host a 30-min kickoff next Tue/Thu.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Partner Programs | Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Developer Experience Bridge: LangChain & LlamaIndex SDK compatibility check

Vanessa — thanks for the clear note and the attachments. ToolSmith is keen to get a formalized certification path for our connector bundle; it helps our enterprise customers move faster. A couple quick clarifying questions before we lock a window:

1) Tracing telemetry: are you expecting OpenTelemetry spans/metrics only, or is there any custom envelope or required attributes (service.name, redispatch.trace_id) we need to inject?
2) SDK variants: we have a thin LangChain adapter and a heavier LlamaIndex plugin — do you want both exercised, or should we prioritize the LangChain path first?
3) Acceptance criteria: is the conformance run pass/fail on strict matching, or do you prefer a graded report (minor/major issues)?

I'll loop in Victor (our integrations lead) if that helps. We're available to kick off the sprint on Feb 22; Tue/Thu mornings (PT) work.

Cheers,
Elena Rossi
Director, Partner Engineering — ToolSmith Integrations
elena@consultify.ai
ToolSmith Inc

On Fri, Feb 12, 2027 at 09:34 AM Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks Elena — quick answers inline and a proposed next step.
>
> 1) Tracing: we expect standard OpenTelemetry spans. Required attributes: service.name, redwood.environment, request.model.variant, and a trace_id (we accept OTel traceparent). We also capture a small set of Redwood-specific tags for routing decisions — those are optional for certification but recommended.
> 2) SDK variants: prioritize the LangChain adapter first (most customers use it), then run a narrow LlamaIndex smoke test.
> 3) Acceptance: graded report preferred: critical (blocking), major (should fix), minor (recommendation). We'll require critical = 0 for certification.
>
> Proposed next step: 30-min kickoff Feb 23 @ 10:00 PT. Can you confirm attendees? I'll add an internal tech owner from runtime.
>
> -Vanessa
>

Subject: Re: Developer Experience Bridge: LangChain & LlamaIndex SDK compatibility check

Elena / team — quick tech checklist from runtime side (this will be the acceptance baseline):

- Initialization: SDK must support an explicit runtime.init(config) that accepts token/region/model_variant and exposes a lifecycle hook for KV cache warmup.
- Tracing: emit OTLP spans; required attributes: service.name, redwood.environment, request.model.variant, span.kind. Include an example of trace propagation when requests hit the fallback path.
- Streaming: sample must demonstrate streaming tokens via chunked responses and show re-assembly in the client adapter.
- Fallbacks: show a simulated capacity fallback and that the SDK surfaces a consistent error code so our routing policy can take effect.
- Security: confirm SDK does not log raw prompts in debug builds; provide redaction knobs.
- Tests: provide a small harness (node/python) that runs 10 canonical prompts; include a latency histogram.

Acceptance format: graded report (Critical / Major / Minor). We will sign-off on certification if Critical == 0 and Major <= 2 after remediation.

I'll volunteer Mateo to join the kickoff as the runtime owner and to help triage any infra questions.

-Kim
